Gopika has been in my batch for three years and is my friend outside it too. Since she missed the qualifying time for the Kolkata half marathon by forty seconds, every cool-down has become the same talk. The cramp at the fifteenth kilometre. The water station she skipped. Whether the watch was wrong. I've listened each time and added my own guesses about the heat.
This week I noticed she leaves these talks slumped, not lighter. We've gone over it nine or ten times and nothing new comes out. Today, instead of another round, I asked gently, "What's one small thing that would help right now?" She was quiet, then said she'd like to plan the next race together. We picked one in March and wrote the first two training weeks on the back of my clipboard sheet.

Avni had heard this at lunch on Monday, over chai on Tuesday, and twice on the walk to the metro. Each time Chinmay went through the same points: his five years, the late nights, the interview he thought went well. And each time his shoulders sank a little lower instead of lifting.

Dear Sabina,

I've been thinking about our phone calls since the flat fell through. Every evening this week we've talked for an hour, and every evening it's the same: the landlord's excuses, the deposit you nearly paid, how you'd already imagined the curtains. I've been right there with you, getting angry at him too.

But after Thursday's call I sat on my bed and noticed I felt worse, not better. And you sounded more tired than on Monday. I don't think going over it again is giving either of us relief.

So I want to ask, gently: what's one small thing that might help now? Maybe looking at two new listings together this Sunday? Or a day off from flats completely, with me and a film?

I'm not going anywhere. I just don't want us stuck in the same loop.

With love,
Nirmala
